_about: WORLD [the job tells the truth, in blood] (rule 208) and [one scale: the blood is the AUTO colour] (rule 254, Paolo 10/26). The numbers a job's stars and blood are read with (slices/bohemia_job_danger.js). ONE CALCULATOR, ONE SCALE: a run is worth what the AUTO button counts it (the fight's own oddsRunValue) and the stars' and the blood's lines are the AUTO colour's own (records/target/bb/ours.json odds_colour: turn and down_value), read from the fight's rules when the page loads; the four copies here (cut_one, cut_three, blood_from, blood_full) are for a modder's eye and the kit's first paint, and gates/the_job_tells_the_truth_gate.js holds them equal to the fight's. The ramp_* rows are rule 255's day-fifty curve (TUNING's numbers). Every other felt number is TUNING's for the one table.

runs.source: OURS: AUTO plays of each fight a job brings, in a worker off the frames (the AUTO button reads 24, rule 144; a job is read once and kept, so more)

prior.source: RULE 254: the job's number is the plain mean of its runs, as the AUTO colour's is (ODDS.shown); the old whisper of doubt ((clean + 1) / (runs + 2)) is gone with the one-in-six reading

cut_one.source: RULE 254 (Paolo 10/26: 'the same calculator as the auto combat'): the AUTO colour's turn (ours.odds_colour.turn, COMBAT's, rule 144(e)): at or over it AUTO is green, the job is ONE star and clean tin. Read from the fight; this copy must equal it. Struck: TUNING's 0.95 on the one-in-six reading (208(a) as amended, struck by 254(c)).

cut_three.source: RULE 254(b): the AUTO colour's down_value (ours.odds_colour.down_value): a run won with men down counts this times the share standing, so at or under it the run the calculator expects has a man down or dead: THREE stars, the deepest blood. Read from the fight; this copy must equal it.

road_per_hour.source: MEASURED by tools/bohemia_world_road_rate.js on the live demo (his computer's screen, 10/26): 260 game hours of travel over 130 trips town to town, 1 crew came for him (the map's forced road events, huntSpawn) and 0 reached him while he kept walking (roads are his, they close only on dirt). The stars count the crews that COME (1 in 260 hours), the honest upper end of the ones that catch him; a party he taps himself is his choice and not counted. Re-run the tool when the road sends more.

blood_from.source: RULE 254: one less the AUTO colour's turn: a danger at or under this is AUTO green, clean tin; just over it is AUTO's first red, the first stage (no clear middle, 144(g)). UI's kit reads it (cfg()). Read from the fight; this copy must equal it.

blood_full.source: RULE 254: one less the AUTO colour's down_value: at this danger and over the button is soaked (the deepest, where the calculator expects men down or dead). Read from the fight; this copy must equal it.

steps.source: the fight's own ODDS_STEPS: a run that has not ended by then counts as not clean

slice_ms.source: the fight's own ODDS_SLICE_MS: a phone with no worker plays six milliseconds a frame

stop_from.source: OURS: a fight plainly lost stops early, after this many plays...

stop_below.source: OURS (measured 10/26, rule 254's gate: at 0.42 after 12 plays, 6 of 221 jobs worth 0.59 to 0.62 stopped and read three stars): ...when its plain mean is under this: a fight that plain is under the deepest line (cut_three 0.50) whatever the next plays say

near_cut.source: OURS: a fight whose read lands between the lines or this close outside them (0.38 to 0.92), where the blood rises, plays on...

runs_more.source: OURS: ...this many more plays at a time...

runs_max.source: OURS (measured 10/26, rule 254's gate: on 32 plays the blood missed the 100-play truth by more than a quarter of its scale on 17 of 221 jobs): ...up to this many, where the blood is read; three times the plays only for the fights that need them

ramp_calm_until.source: TUNING [the day-fifty curve] 10/26 (records/BOHEMIA_TUNING_THE_DAY_FIFTY_CURVE_10_26_26.md, the one table's section U; rule 255(d), a COORDINATOR'S DEFAULT by rule 205 on TUNING's numbers from Battle Brothers' day scaling): through this day the board's worst job is 'could go either way' (worth ramp_floor or more on the AUTO count) and a board holds at most ramp_reds_calm red jobs, the warning

ramp_full_at.source: TUNING [the day-fifty curve] 10/26 (records/BOHEMIA_TUNING_THE_DAY_FIFTY_CURVE_10_26_26.md, the one table's section U; rule 255(d), a COORDINATOR'S DEFAULT by rule 205 on TUNING's numbers from Battle Brothers' day scaling): from ramp_calm_until the floor falls in a straight line to nothing on this day, and the share of red jobs a board may hold grows by the same line to all of it (Paolo 10/26: 'up to 50 days is when shit starts getting difficult')

ramp_floor.source: TUNING [the day-fifty curve] 10/26 (records/BOHEMIA_TUNING_THE_DAY_FIFTY_CURVE_10_26_26.md, the one table's section U; rule 255(d), a COORDINATOR'S DEFAULT by rule 205 on TUNING's numbers from Battle Brothers' day scaling): the floor through the calm days: a job worth under this for the crew he has is not posted, the place posts its next (0.375 at day 20, 0.25 at day 30, 0.125 at day 40). The Lone Wolf, measured: two beasts 38 in 100 on every day to 20, so no beast job reaches him early; 0 turns the ramp off

ramp_reds_calm.source: TUNING [the day-fifty curve] 10/26 (records/BOHEMIA_TUNING_THE_DAY_FIFTY_CURVE_10_26_26.md, the one table's section U; rule 255(d), a COORDINATOR'S DEFAULT by rule 205 on TUNING's numbers from Battle Brothers' day scaling): red jobs (worth under cut_one, the AUTO turn) a board may hold through the calm days; after them round(N x (day - 10) / 40), never under this
